note: "Paper" is fiat currency — dollars and other government-issued notes. In Bitcoin slang, paper money is the thing that loses purchasing power when supply expands. The bar sets the scene in a world where cash already felt thin.

"Print it" is shorthand for monetary expansion: central banks creating new currency units. When money can be printed, prices and debts can be paid with thinner units — the opposite of Bitcoin's fixed 21 million supply.

phrase: double up up on the slots
note: Slots and blackjack stand in for speculative gambling as a come-up path — high variance bets when wages and paper money feel worthless. The verse pairs that risk with later stacking sats: same hunger, different vehicle.
Casino 21 vs protocol 21 — chance versus a rule that does not reset.

In Texas Hold’em a bluff is betting a weak or empty hand hard enough that better hands fold. Fiat governance bluffs with print and confidence; settlement is whoever flinches. Bitcoin settles without the performance.
Poker language (Texas Hold'em) folded into a money flex: bluff like a Texan, then make them pay. Street gambling grammar before the Bitcoin vocabulary arrives.

phrase:
Made it out the hood (let's go)
But I might need security now
note: Exit one risk surface; inherit another. Visible stack, visible target.

Stacking sats means buying small amounts of bitcoin repeatedly. One satoshi is 0.00000001 BTC — one hundred-millionth of a coin. The habit is the culture: accumulate units instead of timing one perfect trade.

phrase: too too much about our bags
note: A bag is a crypto position you hold. Talking too much about your bags is flexing holdings — and risking attention you may not want once the stack is real. The bar is about oversharing the come-up.

phrase: if bitcoin really hit milli (it will)
note: "Milli" here is a million-dollar bitcoin price — the long-running maximalist price target. Parenthetical "it will" is conviction talk: treating the target as inevitable while still hedging the lifestyle fantasy that follows.
"Trad wife" is internet culture for a traditional homemaker role. In the verse it is a lifestyle goal tied to wealth from bitcoin — then immediately undercut by doubt about gold digging.
Gold digging means pursuing a partner for money. The narrator imagines success, then questions motives — freedom from being broke still comes with trust problems.
Self-sovereignty keyword — money, state, and older "set you free" talk in one noun.
Cash-poor, wage-tied; the opposite pole of the prosper flex.
The hook questions whether "freedom from being brokey" is real wealth or an illusion — paper gains, temporary highs, or a lifestyle that can still evaporate. Doubt sits inside the celebration.
Green candles; bullish run.
HODL (from a 2013 forum typo of "hold") means keeping bitcoin through volatility instead of selling. "Hot momentum" is the rush of a rising market while you still refuse to dump the stack.
100,000 sats is 0.001 BTC. Naming stacks in sats is how many holders think day to day — small, countable units rather than whole coins — and "another couple" is the stacking habit continuing.

phrase: It comes down to keeping it
note: Acquisition is only half the game. Keeping bitcoin means not panic-selling, not losing keys, and not spending the stack when fiat pressure hits. Custody and discipline, not just the buy.

phrase: Are you a steward or a brat
note: Custody of the good vs appetite to spoil it.

phrase: you can build or you can rip apart
note: A builder-vs-destroyer fork: create value or sabotage what you care about. Paired with the next bars about cherishing something and fear of self-sabotage — personal discipline framed as construction.
"Cherrish" is the lyric's spelling of cherish. The object is whatever you are trying to protect — the stack, the relationship, the come-up — while the next line threatens to rip it up.
Outflow is money leaving — spending, transfers, or selling. Keeping outflow moderate is cash-flow discipline: don't bleed the stack. In a HODL frame it is living below what the bags could fund.

phrase: How generous I tip a cup
note: Tipping signals having enough to spare. Generosity after the come-up — while "lowkey still scared" of sabotage — is the tension between flex and fear that the freedom is fragile.

phrase: somehow sabotage or mess this up
note: Self-sabotage anxiety after success: the fear that you will blow the stack, the relationship, or the path. Complements the mirage hook — freedom from being brokey can still be lost from the inside.
